You are an expert chemist, your task is to predict the yield of reaction using your experienced chemical yield prediction knowledge.
Please strictly follow the format, no other information can be provided. Given the SMILES string of a Suzuki reaction, the task focuses on predicting reaction yield, specifically whether a reaction is High-yielding (Yes) or Not High-yielding (No), based on the SMILES string representation of each Suzuki reaction. The reactants are separated by '.', which are separated from the product by '>>'. High-yielding reaction means the yield rate of the reaction is above 70. You will be provided with several examples molecules. Please answer with only Yes or No.The Reaction is as follows
CC(=O)O~CC(=O)O~[Pd].CC(C)(C)P(C1=CC=C[CH]1)C(C)(C)C.CC(C)(C)P(C1=CC=C[CH]1)C(C)(C)C.CCc1cccc(CC)c1.CO.Cc1ccc2c(cnn2C2CCCCO2)c1B(O)O.Ic1ccc2ncccc2c1.O.[Fe]>>Cc1ccc2c(cnn2C2CCCCO2)c1-c1ccc2ncccc2c1You have to output your judge, which is "Yes" or "No", and exactly follow the output format, which is as follows:
{"answer": "The answer you judge"}. I don't need any explanation, you just need to output your judgment in the format.

Please use your tools to analyze and solve this problem accurately.

1. [ ] Identify the reaction features and retrieve empirical Suzuki conditions or analogous evidence.
2. [ ] Assess whether the reaction is likely to exceed 70% yield and return the required JSON.

Tool call: go_search_agent
Tool call input: {'knowledge_bases': ['chemistry'], 'search_rounds_budget': 2, 'search_target': 'Assess likely yield category (>70% yes/no) for Suzuki coupling represented by reactants: heteroaryl boronic acid (pyrazole-fused aryl B(OH)2) plus iodoquinoline, Pd(OAc)2, bulky di-tert-butyl cyclopentadienyl phosphine ligand (two equivalents), 1,2-diethylbenzene solvent with methanol/water, iron additive; product biaryl. Find analogous reaction-condition records or evidence of expected yield.'}

The ORD search found no exact record for the specified reaction and conditions. Product-similarity analogues report yields from 43% to 96.9%, but differ in substrates and reaction conditions, so they do not reliably predict this reaction’s yield. **Assessment: >70% — No (low confidence).**
